title: Nav Status Icon Legend
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
Material for MkDocs
Navigation
Status Lifecycle
Accessibility
description: A p5.js legend and matching quiz for the five MicroSim nav status icons (scaffold, built, implemented, instrumented, approved). A mock navigation sidebar shows each icon with its real color and tooltip text; clicking an icon shows its meaning, the batch lifecycle state that usually produces it and its contrast ratio on a light or dark sidebar.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Reading nav status icons and mapping them to the batch lifecycle
learningObjectives: The learner will match each nav status icon and color to its meaning and to the batch lifecycle state that usually produces it.
prerequisites: Front matter status in Material for MkDocs

accessibility.notes: Keys 1-5 select a nav row; the three icon shapes (circle, broadcast, check) and text labels mean color is not the only cue; the panel reports WCAG contrast ratios

controls.label: Nav rows 1-5
controls.purpose: Hover for the nav tooltip; click to show meaning, lifecycle state and contrast

controls.label: Quiz me / Stop quiz
controls.purpose: Hide labels and tooltips, shuffle icons and ask the learner to click the icon for a description

controls.label: Next question
controls.purpose: Advance the quiz after an answer

controls.label: Dark mode
controls.purpose: Switch the mock sidebar to a dark background

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Legend exploration followed by a matching quiz
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Labeled legend with click-for-detail and matching quiz
keyQuestions: Which two nav statuses both come from the validated lifecycle state?
Which status is set by sync-status.py rather than the batch pipeline?
Why do the icons differ in shape as well as color?
commonMisconceptions: Nav status and sim-status.json status are the same list
assessmentOpportunities: Mapping a lifecycle state to a nav status
Explaining the built versus approved distinction
